comments.note: A07 — Authentication Failures (Low). File: src/VideoIndexer.App/ViewModels/LogonViewModel.cs. SubmitCommand has no rate-limiting, delay, or lockout counter at the view-model layer. For a local single-user desktop app this is acceptable (no network exposure), but if the app were extended to a shared/multi-user scenario, unconstrained repeated submission attempts would be a concern. Recommended: if the threat model ever expands, add a short backoff or attempt counter in ShellViewModel.LogOnAsync.

A02 — Cryptographic Failures (Info). File: src/VideoIndexer.App/ViewModels/LogonViewModel.cs line 32. The password is captured in the local variable 'var pw = Password' (a .NET string) before being cleared. .NET strings are immutable and not zero-wiped from the heap; the value remains in memory until garbage collected. This is an inherent .NET limitation and cannot be avoided without using char[] or SecureString (which Avalonia's TextBox does not natively support). The early clear ('Password = string.Empty') before the async call is good defensive practice, but does not constitute a secure wipe. Low practical risk for a local desktop app with no memory-dump attack surface exposure in the threat model.

A02 / A05 — Positive findings. PasswordChar='\u25cf' is applied to the TextBox in LogonView.axaml, masking the password on screen. Password is cleared from the view-model property before the delegate call (SubmitAsync lines 32-33), minimising in-memory exposure window. CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals is used in PasswordService.VerifyAsync (WP-011, previously audited). All three security-positive patterns are present.
